title: How do you guarantee an operation is applied only once?
description: Learn idempotency patterns, how to design APIs and event consumers that survive retries, and why exactly-once semantics usually require application-level design.

data.text: In distributed systems, networks fail, timeouts happen, and messages are redelivered. The question is not whether a request will be retried, but whether your system treats a second attempt as a new operation or as a duplicate.

An operation is idempotent if calling it once or many times has the same observable effect. A payment of $50 is naturally idempotent if your system records that paymentId X was already processed and ignores subsequent calls with the same ID.

terms.definition: A unique identifier the client generates so the server can recognize duplicate requests.
A messaging guarantee that a message is delivered once and only once. In practice, this requires both the broker and the consumer to cooperate.
A messaging guarantee that a message is delivered one or more times. This is the common default and the reason idempotency is needed.

data.title: Common approaches
items: Idempotency keys on write APIs—client sends a unique key, server stores the result keyed by that ID
Database unique constraints—let the database reject duplicates with a clear error code
Outbox pattern—write the event and the business change in the same transaction so neither is lost
Deduplication window—track processed message IDs for a rolling time window and skip repeats

data.title: Client-generated keys
data.text: Idempotency keys must be generated by the client, not the server. A server-generated ID does not help if the client cannot correlate retries with the original request.

data.title: Idempotent payment API
data.content: A mobile app sends a payment request with an idempotency key generated from the order ID. The server checks a processed_keys table before charging. If the user retries after a network timeout, the server returns the original result instead of charging twice.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Design every write operation as if it will be retried
Use idempotency keys for external APIs and payment flows
Combine outbox patterns with deduplication for event-driven systems
